title: Credit Controller
description:
Join a well-established Poole-based retail organisation as a Credit Controller. Known for a friendly and dynamic culture, our client prides itself on their commitment to quality and team development. Conveniently located in Poole, Dorset with easy access and a professional but relaxed work environment, this company values punctuality, staff engagement, and continuous learning. This role offers an immediate start, flexible hours in the mornings, and a chance to be part of a reputable retail sector leader.

What will the Credit Controller role involve?
- Managing a portfolio of customer accounts, ensuring timely and accurate processing of sales invoices and receipts, contributing to smooth financial operations
- Engaging with customers via email and phone to facilitate collections and resolve account queries, supporting cash flow targets
- Collaborating with internal teams to ensure billing accuracy and efficient account management, fostering strong stakeholder relationships
- Assisting with basic financial analysis and reporting, helping to optimise collection strategies
- Maintaining meticulous records, adhering to company policies, and supporting continuous process improvement initiatives

Suitable Candidate for the Credit Controller vacancy:
- Proven experience in sales ledger, credit control, or accounts receivable functions, ideally within retail or a similar sector
- Effective communication skills, both written and verbal, with a confident telephone manner
- Strong organisational skills with attention to detail and the ability to prioritise tasks effectively
- Proficient with Excel; training on company-specific software will be provided
- Positive attitude, punctuality, and the desire to learn and develop within a finance role

Additional benefits and information for the role of Credit Controller:
- Flexible working hours in the morning to suit your routinea

- Opportunities to gain experience in credit control and finance operations within a thriving retail business

title: Personal Assistant
description:
Personal Assistant

Poole, Dorset Full-Time Permanent Up to £40,000

The Opportunity

We are recruiting on behalf of a well-established, family-run manufacturing business based in Poole, Dorset, supplying high-quality iron components to the global automotive industry.

The business is looking for an experienced Personal Assistant to provide proactive organisational and administrative support to senior members of the Board, with a particular focus on the Managing Director and President.

This is a key role for someone who enjoys being at the centre of a business, building strong working relationships and confidently managing competing priorities. You will become a trusted member of the existing team, helping ensure senior leaders are well organised and the day-to-day operation of the Head Office runs smoothly and professionally.

Key Responsibilities
- Proactively manage business and, where required, personal calendars for senior executives, resolving diary conflicts and prioritising requests.
- Coordinate documents requiring Executive review, signature or approval, ensuring deadlines are met and records are securely maintained.
- Arrange complex domestic and international travel, including flights, transfers, hotels, car parking, visas, itineraries and other local arrangements.
- Support international travel coordination across the wider business as required.
- Act as a key point of contact for external visitors, arranging transport and accommodation.
- Monitor travel plans and respond quickly to delays, cancellations and last-minute changes, providing practical solutions and clear communication.
- Coordinate key company events and meetings, including senior management reviews, long-service events and technical conferences.
- Liaise with stakeholders across the UK and internationally, as well as hotels, venues, transport providers and other suppliers, to ensure events run smoothly.
- Process and reconcile expenses, including travel-related expenditure and supporting documentation.
- Administer the Company's private medical healthcare scheme and act as the principal point of contact for employees.
- Arrange annual medical assessments for senior managers, coordinating appointments with medical providers and individuals.
- Take responsibility for the smooth and professional operation of Reception.
- Provide general office administration and wider support to the business as required.

The Candidate

We are looking for an experienced Personal Assistant, Executive Assistant or Senior Administrator who is comfortable supporting senior executives and managing a varied workload.

You will ideally have:
- Proven experience supporting senior executives or senior management.
- Excellent organisational skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and changing deadlines.
- Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the confidence to build relationships at all levels.
- The ability to handle confidential and sensitive information with complete discretion and professionalism.
- Strong attention to detail and good proficiency in Microsoft Office.
- A calm, adaptable and proactive approach to problem solving.
- A flexible, hands-on attitude and willingness to support both business and personal matters where required.
- The confidence to work independently and anticipate what senior leaders need before being asked.

What's on Offer
- Salary up to £40,000
- Permanent position
- 4.5-day working week
- Monday Thursday: 8:00am 4:30pm
- Friday: 8:00am 12:30pm
- Office-based in Poole, Dorset
- Potential flexibility around working hours, to be discussed at interview
- Opportunity to join an established and growing international manufacturing business
- Start date: December

Occasional out-of-hours support may be required to assist with time-zone differences when senior managers are travelling.

If this role is of interest please press apply or reach out to Ryan Guy on (phone number removed) or (url removed)

title: Patient Administrator
company: University Hospitals Dorset NHS Foundation Trust
advertiser_name: University Hospitals Dorset NHS Foundation Trust
description: This full time Outpatient Administrator role provides a caring service to our patients at UHD. The role involves providing an appointment booking service, liaising with Consultants, medical secretaries, the Primary Care Trust and other departments in the Trust. This job will be based at Royal Bournemouth, Canford House, Wallisdown Road or Poole Hospital - Longfleet Road. There will be a requirement to be flexible to work across all sites at certain times. The Administrators book patient appointments from referral letters and are the first point of contact on the patient's pathway through the hospital. Interview: 9th November To succeed in this role you will need to possess good communication skills and have a passion to deliver outstanding service to our patients. Accuracy and attention to detail are essential requirements together with the ability to multitask in a busy environment. Good team skills are also an essential requirement. This role involves data input, providing an efficient telephone service and assisting patients with their appointments. You may also be required to provide a welcoming receptionist service to our patients attending the Outpatient clinics, which includes checking patient's details, booking follow up appointments and ensuring the clinics are ready for the clinicians and patients. The Outpatients Department is an exciting place to work in and for many patient's the 'window of the hospital'. We look after approximately 200,000 patients per annum and aim to provide an excellent and caring service at all times. It is a friendly environment with the administrators providing clerical support to our clinical colleagues. The department operates between the hours of 07.30 and 18.00 and staff work on a rotational shift basis. Base Location: Poole Hospital - Longfleet Road, Canford House - Royal Bournemouth To understand the role in more detail please read the full job description and person specification documents which are attached to this advert.

title: ESR Administrator
company: Dorset HealthCare University NHS Foundation Trust
advertiser_name: Dorset HealthCare University NHS Foundation Trust
description: We are looking for a proactive and highly motivated ESR Administrator to join our team during an exciting period of growth, innovation and preparation for the future workforce solution. We are dedicated to enhancing and expanding the ESR system and services we provide to all staff at Dorset HealthCare University Foundation Trust. As the primary workforce management system used across the NHS, ESR plays a pivotal role in our operations. By joining our team, you will contribute to driving positive change within the trust, helping us deliver improved services and support to all employees. The ideal candidate will have previous experience with ESR. As an ESR Administrator you will provide essential support to our staff by managing access and training needs via the service desk, maintaining, reporting, and reviewing accounts, roles, work structure's and data quality within ESR. Please note visa sponsorship for this role is unfortunately not available. Ensure you hold valid right to work in the UK and will not require sponsorship if successful. You will play a key role in delivering and maintaining Manager, Administrator, Supervisor and Employee Self-Service. Optimising existing system functionalities, and implementing new features and functionality across various departments and teams. The role of ESR Administrator will include providing training needs and ongoing support to all staff and their use of Self-Service, and working cooperatively and maintaining close working relationships with our other trusts departments, particularly HR, Payroll, Finance and Rostering. It is essential that you have excellent IT Skills, including Microsoft Office, Teams and Outlook. Previous experience of ESR and Self-Service is desirable but not essential as full training will be provided. You must be methodical, organised, and work to a high standard with a flexible approach and understanding of the need to respond/deliver work across a diverse area within tight timescales. The role is based at our Dorset HealthCare HQ site in Poole and a weekly presence is required on site. There may also be the need for occasional travel to our other sites around Dorset. The post holder may be required to work flexibly to meet the needs of the service. For the main duties and responsibilities for this role please read the attached job description and person specification. When completing your application please ensure your supporting statement reflects the criteria set out in these documents by showing how your experience and skills apply to this post. We understand that AI can be a useful tool when completing your application. However, we are seeing an increasing over-reliance of AI tools, which can negatively affect your application as it reduces a candidates individuality, and makes it difficult for us to gain a clear and authentic understanding of your experience, skills, and in turn your suitability for the role. All submissions must be truthful and if you do use AI, it should only be used to enhance your application and not create your supporting statement in its entirety. Your supporting statement should be in your own words and must accurately reflect your personal experience and achievements. Where we have concerns that AI has been used to generate content that misrepresents your experience and suitability for the role, we may withdraw your application. As part of our vision to have a skilled, diverse and caring workforce, Dorset HealthCare offers support for people getting into work. We offer an employability service to support individuals with application writing, interview skills and other employment support. If you would like or know of anyone who would value this support, please do contact dhc.wideningparticipation@nhs.net
